newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures lower at noon after JGB fall.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures lower at noon after JGB fall.

text.p: The key December three-month Euroyen interest rate futures had edged down by midday on Tuesday, dragged lower by a sharp fall in Japanese government bond futures.
The key June JGB futures contract fell to 123.10 by midday against its Monday close of 123.66, mainly on sales of June JGB futures put options, bond traders said.

This, with lingering influence from comments last week by senior MOF official Eisuke Sakakibara, helped push key December Euroyen futures as low as 98.85 before ending the morning at 98.86. Its high was 98.90 and turnover 37,531 contracts.
Sakakibara was quoted as telling Le Monde last week that a rise in Japan's official discount rate should be expected in the coming year.

One city bank dealer said he felt that 98.85 was likely to become support for now, but added that further moves depend largely on what happens to JGBs in afternoon trade. "This morning's selling was somewhat more active than expected, and concern about the downside is definitely increasing," he said.
A trust bank dealer said technical support was likely around 98.86, although a dip as low as 98.82-83 is possible should JGBs fall even further. Resistance is seen at 98.90.
In the interbank market, key overnight call money was traded at around 0.52 percent, up from Monday's 0.51 percent, as demand rises ahead of the month-end.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) injected a net 600 billion yen into the money market in its regular morning operation, in line with market expectations, against a net shortfall of 600 billion yen.
The BOJ's credit stance has been neutral since the start of the current bank reserve period.
